nodes.label: Customer
nodes.description: A shopper who has added items to their cart and checks out.

nodes.label: Cart summary
nodes.description: The line items, quantities, and running total the customer reviews before checkout.

tactical.explanation: CartPage renders the session cart from CartService.GetCart(); the checkout button is disabled while the cart is empty.

fields.name: lineItems
fields.derivation: The cart lines the customer added, projected from persisted order-item rows.

fields.name: runningTotal
fields.derivation: Sum of each line's amount; computed for display and never persisted for the cart itself.
fields.notes: Client-side sum; no server aggregate confirms it.

nodes.label: PlaceOrder
nodes.description: Customer submits the cart as an order.

tactical.explanation: Checkout button calls OrderService.placeOrder(cart, customerId), which validates stock and payment before creating the order.

nodes.label: Order
nodes.description: A customer order: header plus line items, with status and total. Emits an event when placed.

tactical.explanation: OrderService.placeOrder inserts an orders row and order_items rows in one transaction, status='Placed', then returns the order id.

fields.name: orderId
fields.derivation: Database-assigned identity of the orders row, returned to the caller.

fields.name: status
fields.derivation: Lifecycle state of the order; set to 'Placed' on successful checkout.

fields.name: total
fields.derivation: Order total charged to the customer, stored in cents.

fields.name: placedAt
fields.derivation: When the order was committed; not stored on the row, taken as the transaction time.
fields.notes: No dedicated column; inferred from commit ordering.

nodes.label: Every line must have stock available
nodes.description: An order is rejected if any line item's requested quantity exceeds on-hand stock.

tactical.explanation: placeOrder loops items and throws OutOfStockError when InventoryRepo.onHand(sku) < qty, before any write.

nodes.label: Payment must authorize before the order is created
nodes.description: The order is only written after the payment gateway authorizes the charge.

tactical.explanation: placeOrder awaits PaymentGateway.authorize(total); a declined result throws PaymentDeclinedError before the insert.

nodes.label: OrderPlaced
nodes.description: A new order now exists in status Placed with an authorized payment.

tactical.explanation: The committed orders + order_items write; placeOrder returns the order and the UI navigates to the confirmation page.

nodes.label: Payment gateway
nodes.description: Third-party payment processor. Authorizes and captures card charges over HTTPS.

tactical.explanation: PaymentGateway wraps the processor's REST API; authorize() places a hold, capture() settles it after fulfillment.

nodes.label: Whenever an order is placed, reserve its stock
nodes.description: Placing an order immediately decrements on-hand stock for each line so the same unit can't be sold twice.

tactical.explanation: Inline after commit, placeOrder calls InventoryService.reserve(items) — a separate store (inventory) with its own failure window, hence a policy-issued command.

nodes.label: ReserveStock
nodes.description: Decrement on-hand stock for each ordered line.

tactical.explanation: InventoryService.reserve updates inventory.on_hand per sku; failures are logged and do not roll back the order (a hotspot).

nodes.label: Inventory
nodes.description: On-hand stock per SKU. Decremented when an order reserves stock.

tactical.explanation: inventory table keyed by sku; reserve() is the only write path in this flow.

fields.name: sku
fields.derivation: Stock-keeping unit identifying the product line.

fields.name: onHand
fields.derivation: Units currently available; decremented when an order reserves stock.

nodes.label: StockReserved
nodes.description: On-hand stock has been decremented for the order's lines.

tactical.explanation: Aftermath of the inventory update; nothing subscribes downstream in this toy model.

nodes.label: app-sql-01
nodes.description: Primary OLTP SQL Server instance backing the shop.

tactical.explanation: The Default connection string in config names this server/instance; every repository connects through it.

nodes.label: shop
nodes.description: The shop application database (orders, order lines, inventory).

nodes.label: orders
nodes.description: Order headers: one row per placed order.

tactical.explanation: placeOrder issues INSERT INTO orders (status, total_cents) inside the checkout transaction.

nodes.label: order_items
nodes.description: Order lines: one row per item on an order.

tactical.explanation: placeOrder bulk-inserts order_items (qty, amount_cents) for each cart line in the same transaction.
reserve() runs UPDATE inventory SET on_hand = on_hand - @qty WHERE sku = @sku per line.

flows.name: Customer places an order
flows.summary: The customer reviews their cart and checks out. The order is created only after stock is confirmed and the payment gateway authorizes the charge; on success, stock is reserved in a separate step whose failure does not roll back the order.
flows.trigger: Checkout button on the cart page

hotspots.label: Stock reservation is not atomic with order creation
hotspots.description: Reservation runs after the order transaction commits, in a separate store, and its failure is only logged. An order can exist for stock that was never decremented, so the same unit can be oversold. Human question: should reserve() share the order transaction, or should a failed reservation cancel/flag the order?

tactical.explanation: OrderService.placeOrder commits the order at line 61, then calls InventoryService.reserve at line 63 outside any transaction; reserve swallows failures (InventoryService.ts:31).
